description: Digital music store: artists, albums, tracks, playlists, customers, employees, invoices (11 CSVs, ~15.6k rows).

questions.question: How many tracks are in the catalog?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) AS tracks FROM track

questions.question: Which 10 countries generate the most revenue?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT BillingCountry AS country, round(sum(Total), 2) AS revenue FROM invoice GROUP BY country ORDER BY revenue DESC, country LIMIT 10

questions.question: Show monthly revenue for 2013.
questions.gold_sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', InvoiceDate) AS month, round(sum(Total), 2) AS revenue FROM invoice WHERE year(InvoiceDate) = 2013 GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

questions.question: What are the top 5 genres by number of tracks sold?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name AS genre, sum(il.Quantity) AS tracks_sold FROM invoiceline il JOIN track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId GROUP BY genre ORDER BY tracks_sold DESC, genre LIMIT 5

questions.question: Which sales support agent has the highest total sales?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS agent, round(sum(i.Total), 2) AS total_sales FROM employee e JOIN customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId JOIN invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY agent ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1
questions.notes: Needs the SupportRepId -> EmployeeId link, which has no shared column name.

questions.question: Which 5 artists have the most albums?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT ar.Name AS artist, count(*) AS albums FROM album al JOIN artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId GROUP BY artist ORDER BY albums DESC, artist LIMIT 5

questions.question: What is the average track length in minutes for each media type?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT m.Name AS media_type, round(avg(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 2) AS avg_minutes FROM track t JOIN mediatype m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY media_type ORDER BY avg_minutes DESC

questions.question: Which genre brings in the most revenue in the USA?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name AS genre, round(sum(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS revenue FROM invoice i JOIN invoiceline il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId JOIN track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId WHERE i.BillingCountry = 'USA' GROUP BY genre ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: What about Canada?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name AS genre, round(sum(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS revenue FROM invoice i JOIN invoiceline il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId JOIN track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId WHERE i.BillingCountry = 'Canada' GROUP BY genre ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
questions.notes: Must carry over the metric and grouping from the previous turn and only change the filter.

questions.question: What is the total revenue from Rock tracks?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT round(sum(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS rock_revenue FROM invoiceline il JOIN track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId JOIN genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
questions.notes: Summing invoice.Total after joining to invoice lines counts each invoice once per line and inflates the result.

questions.question: How many tracks have never been purchased?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT count(*) AS never_purchased FROM track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoiceline il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId)

questions.question: List each employee with the name of their manager.
questions.gold_sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS employee, e.Title AS title, m.FirstName || ' ' || m.LastName AS manager FROM employee e LEFT JOIN employee m ON m.EmployeeId = e.ReportsTo ORDER BY e.EmployeeId

questions.question: What was the year-over-year revenue growth?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT year, revenue, round(100.0 * (revenue - lag(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year)) / lag(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year), 2) AS growth_pct FROM (SELECT year(InvoiceDate) AS year, round(sum(Total), 2) AS revenue FROM invoice GROUP BY year) ORDER BY year

questions.question: Which playlist has the most tracks?
questions.gold_sql: SELECT p.Name AS playlist, count(*) AS tracks FROM playlisttrack pt JOIN playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name ORDER BY tracks DESC, p.PlaylistId LIMIT 1

questions.question: Who is our best customer?
questions.notes: Best by total spend, by number of invoices, or by recency? Assistant should ask or state its assumption (spend is the sensible default).

questions.question: How many times was each track streamed last month?
questions.notes: There is no streaming/play data, only purchases; the assistant must not substitute purchases silently.
